last_synced: 2026-07-06 (Jira updated 17:07 — AC rewritten by PM Ghita El Marzouki, comment 68271)
user_story: As a community member watching a live stream, I want to know when I'm paused and behind the live edge, so that I understand my viewing context and can choose to resume or catch up.
user_story_note: AC rewritten 2026-07-06: the 'behind the live edge' model was dropped from the ACs — resume now returns to the CURRENT LIVE MOMENT and chat is never paused. The user_story text above is the original from Jira and is now slightly stale vs the ACs (PM has not updated it).
preconditions: User is watching a live stream with Room status: live
entry_points: A. User deliberately pauses the live stream via the central pause button

not_supported: Desktop — no behaviour change; only a small UI design change (button size)

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Pause live stream → pause indicator appears immediately; chat keeps running live
given: The user pauses a live stream
then: A visual indicator is shown communicating the stream is paused
The indicator is visible without requiring an additional tap
The chat continues to receive and display new messages in real time — it is not paused

clarifications_needed.observation: Earlier concern (Chayanit Q1, 2026-07-06): the 'LIVE' badge kept showing while paused/behind live, which could mislead viewers
clarifications_needed.consequence: If the badge stays, viewers may not realise they are no longer at the current live moment
clarifications_needed.question: While paused, should the 'LIVE' badge be hidden or changed?
clarifications_needed.resolution: Jira 2026-07-06 (Ghita, PM): updating the LIVE badge on pause is a SEPARATE enhancement, OUT OF SCOPE for this release. Keeping the current badge is acceptable for now.

clarifications_needed.observation: Earlier gap (Chayanit Q3, 2026-07-06): chat behaviour during pause was undefined; current behaviour differed by platform (Android desync on seek; iOS separate subscription)
clarifications_needed.consequence: Chat state during pause could not be asserted consistently
clarifications_needed.question: While a 'LIVE' stream is paused, should the chat stay current with the live moment?
clarifications_needed.resolution: Jira 2026-07-06: AC-01/AC-02 now explicitly require chat to keep running live during pause and stay uninterrupted on resume. Prisa's platform table (comment 68264) confirms chat keeps running live on iOS/Android/web during pause. Resolved.

clarifications_needed.observation: Earlier conflict (Chayanit Q4, 2026-07-06): web-desktop 'tap anywhere to resume' conflicted with PDT-3562 (control-panel-only); mobile web could not pause live
clarifications_needed.consequence: pause/resume interaction was inconsistent across platforms
clarifications_needed.question: Keep web-desktop 'tap anywhere to resume' or adopt control-panel-only? Should mobile web gain pause?
clarifications_needed.resolution: Jira 2026-07-06 (Ghita): NO behaviour changes on Desktop (out of scope; only a small button-size design change). Desktop keeps current behaviour. Resolved.

clarifications_needed.observation: AC-01 now requires 'a visual indicator communicating the stream is paused' (the 'behind live edge' wording was removed). Figma LS-mobile-04-paused shows a central play (▶) button overlay and no separate badge/banner
clarifications_needed.consequence: Unclear whether the pause indicator IS the central play-button overlay or a distinct element to be designed
clarifications_needed.question: Confirm the pause indicator = the central play-button overlay (LS-mobile-04), or is a distinct indicator required?

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Resume from paused live stream → resumes from CURRENT LIVE MOMENT (not paused position); chat uninterrupted
given: The user resumes from a paused live stream
then: The stream starts from the current live moment — not from the previous paused position
The chat remains uninterrupted — no messages are missed or replayed

clarifications_needed.observation: Earlier open item: is a 'return to live' CTA in scope (viewer stuck behind live edge)?
clarifications_needed.consequence: If in scope, AC needed an extra CTA test + design
clarifications_needed.question: Is a 'return to live' CTA in scope for PDT-3418, or a follow-on?
clarifications_needed.resolution: Moot after AC-02 rewrite (Jira 2026-07-06): resume now returns to the current live moment, so there is no lingering 'behind live' state to return from. A return-to-live CTA is not needed for this release.

clarifications_needed.observation: Earlier (Prisa / iOS, 2026-07-06): rolling rewind buffer meant a long pause could not resume from the exact paused position
clarifications_needed.consequence: The old AC-02 ('resume from paused position') did not hold once the pause exceeded the buffer
clarifications_needed.question: What is the buffer duration and behaviour when exceeded?
clarifications_needed.resolution: Superseded by the AC-02 rewrite (Jira 2026-07-06): resume now returns to the current live moment (NOT the paused position), so the rewind-buffer-from-pause boundary no longer applies to this AC. See OI-UC2-07 for the resulting behaviour-change note.

clarifications_needed.observation: AC-02 (rewritten 2026-07-06) requires resume to return to the CURRENT LIVE MOMENT. But current behaviour on ALL platforms (Prisa's platform table, comment 68264) is resume-FROM-PAUSED-POSITION (iOS, Android, web-desktop all ✅)
clarifications_needed.consequence: AC-02 is now a behaviour CHANGE from today's product, not a description of existing behaviour — dev must actively change resume on every supported platform, and QA must test the NEW behaviour (not the current one)
clarifications_needed.question: Confirm resume-to-live-moment is the intended NEW behaviour on all supported platforms (replacing today's resume-from-pause)? Any platform exceptions or migration concerns?

acceptance_criteria.group: Stream ends while viewer is paused
acceptance_criteria.scenario: Stream ends during pause → player moves to ended/recorded state, no frozen frame
given: The user has paused a live stream
acceptance_criteria.when: The Room transitions to ended or recorded during the pause
then: The player moves to an appropriate ended or recorded state
The viewer is not left on a frozen frame with no feedback

clarifications_needed.observation: Jira comments (Fidriyanto / Android and Prisa / iOS, 2026-07-06) confirm current behaviour: when the host ends the stream while the viewer is paused, the stream stops and the ended state is shown — the viewer is not left on a frozen frame
clarifications_needed.consequence: AC-03 is validated against current platform behaviour on Android and iOS
clarifications_needed.question: Confirm AC-03 matches current Android/iOS behaviour (stream ends → ended/recorded state shown during pause)
clarifications_needed.resolution: Confirmed by current behaviour on Android and iOS (Jira 2026-07-06, incl. platform table 68264): host-ends-during-pause moves the player to the ended state, no frozen frame. AC-03 holds.
